claims.text: University of Bristol uses a four-category system for AI use in assessments: Category 1 (prohibited - no AI use), Category 2 (minimal - spelling/grammar only, default), Category 3 (selective - certain tasks as specified), and Category 4 (integral - AI required for assessment).

evidence.quote: Category 1: prohibited (not allowed) - You cannot use AI tools at all, including spelling and grammar checkers. Category 2: minimal (a little) - You can use AI tools for spelling and grammar check. You can use it for rewording occasional phrases, but not sentences, large parts of text or paragraphs. Category 3: selective (certain tasks) - AI tools can be used in certain ways. Your lecturer will tell you what you can use it for. Category 4: integral (important) - AI tools are needed for the assessment.
evidence.title: https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/academic-advice/using-artificial-intelligence/

claims.text: Using artificial intelligence (AI) in assessments and for studying

evidence.quote:
The use of AI during an assessment or studying will depend on the learning objectives, course and school. For advice around how and when to use AI, contact your lecturer, school, personal tutor or supervisor.
If you use AI in other ways than what the lecturer says, it may be seen as contract cheating.
This guidance is for undergraduates and PGT students.

You cannot use AI tools at all, including spelling and grammar checkers.

AI tools are needed for the assessment. You will be told which tools to use and in what capacity.

evidence.quote:

claims.text: Guidance for PGR students on the use of AI tools in thesis writing

evidence.quote:
To be awarded a research degree, you must meet several key standards in your research training. One of these is the ability to write about your research in your own words. This critical research skill is tested through your thesis and through your annual progress monitoring (APM) reports. For this reason, you are not permitted to use generative AI tools to write any text that is used in your thesis or in your APM reports. This guidance sets out how AI tools can be used.
You must consider whether it is safe to input confidential, sensitive or personal information into a generative AI tool. Make sure that you seek advice from your supervisors.

15.1. Students may appeal the decision of an Academic Misconduct panel on one or more of the following grounds: New supporting evidence, relevant to the finding of academic misconduct, is available that could make a difference to the outcome and which the student was unable, for good reason, to disclose at the time of the panel. claims.text: University of Bristol uses a four-category system for AI use in assessments: Category 1 (prohibited - no AI use), Category 2 (minimal - spelling/grammar only, default), Category 3 (selective - certain tasks as specified), and Category 4 (integral - AI required for assessment).

evidence.quote: Category 1: prohibited (not allowed) - You cannot use AI tools at all, including spelling and grammar checkers. Category 2: minimal (a little) - You can use AI tools for spelling and grammar check. You can use it for rewording occasional phrases, but not sentences, large parts of text or paragraphs. Category 3: selective (certain tasks) - AI tools can be used in certain ways. Your lecturer will tell you what you can use it for. Category 4: integral (important) - AI tools are needed for the assessment.
evidence.title: https://www.bristol.ac.uk/students/support/academic-advice/using-artificial-intelligence/
